:::{#exm-logarithm}
#### Logarithms to other bases

- $\log_2 8 = 3$ (@def-logarithm),
  because $2^3 = 8$.
- $\log_{10} 0.01 = -2$,
  because $10^{-2} = 0.01$.

The [graph](functions.qmd#def-graph) of $\log_2 x$ passes through $(8, 3)$,
the first of these two facts.

```{r}
#| code-fold: true
#| echo: !expr knitr::is_html_output()
#| message: false
#| warning: false
#| fig-alt: >-
#|   The graph of the logarithm to base 2 for x from 0.1 to 10. The curve
#|   rises steeply near 0, crosses the horizontal axis at x = 1, and keeps
#|   rising more slowly. A dot marks the point (8, 3).

x <- seq(0.1, 10, length.out = 200)
curve <- data.frame(x = x, y = log2(x))
marked <- data.frame(x = 8, y = 3)

log_plot <- ggplot2::ggplot(curve, ggplot2::aes(x = x, y = y)) +
  ggplot2::geom_line() +
  ggplot2::geom_point(data = marked, colour = "firebrick", size = 2) +
  ggplot2::labs(x = "x", y = "log base 2 of x")

log_plot
```

:::
